_comment: Own Hub — Firestore indexes and, more importantly, index EXEMPTIONS.
Firestore indexes every field automatically, including each non-array subfield
of a map and the elements of arrays. That means §2 rule 11 — nothing is ranked
by weight, weight lost, or followers — is FALSE in a deployed project unless the
exemptions below exist, no matter what the application code says. Four separate
A fieldOverride with an empty 'indexes' array disables automatic indexing for
that field, so the forbidden query cannot be executed rather than merely being
denied. These are deployment artifacts, not tuning: deploy them with the rules,
and assert after deploy that the forbidden query fails.

indexes._why: G10 community feed. The whole feed is one query per audience chunk; fan-out happens on READ, never on write (spine C9).
G12 coach roster, paginated 20 per page. The only hot-path composite in the coach app.
G11 the coach's enquiry queue. Declared openly rather than claimed away.
G10 a woman's own posts, newest first, for her profile grid.

S13. expire_stale_reviews: verification_flags where state == PENDING_REVIEW and slaExpiresAt < now. Equality plus a range on a second field needs a composite; without it the hourly SLA job fails on every run and no stale review ever becomes RETRY_REQUIRED.
The reviewer queue (list_verification_flags and tools/review_queue.py): open flags, oldest first, so the woman who has waited longest is called first.

fieldOverrides._why: RULE 11. Sets are embedded in the session document (spine C2), so every element of the array is auto-indexed — including actualWeight. Without this, 'order sessions by weight lifted' is a query that simply works.
RULE 11. Her weight. Private to her, never compared, never ranked — enforced here rather than in a repository method someone can bypass.
RULE 11. Body measurements, same reasoning.
RULE 11. Personal bests are hers; a league table of loads is exactly what this product refuses to build.
RULE 11. Follower counts are DISPLAYED, never ranked (HANDOFF rule 11). Leaving this indexed makes 'most followed women' a one-line query.
RULE 11. Likes and comments on a post. Ordering by them turns a community into a leaderboard.
RULE 11. A follow-up's cost summary carries counted weeks and sessions; ranking by it ranks women by effort.
RULE 11. Group size. Ordering groups by membership makes the biggest room the default, which is the opposite of what a beginner needs.

RULE 11, and the sharpest case: a client result carries her before/after numbers. Indexed, 'rank coaches by client weight lost' is a query that just works — which is precisely the marketing this product refuses.
PDPL. Cycle settings must not be queryable across users at all, so that 'find every pregnant woman' is unexecutable rather than merely denied.
PDPL. Period entries, same reasoning.
PDPL. Daily symptoms live on the check-in; no field of it may be queryable across women.
PDPL, as above.
PDPL, as above.
COST, not a rule. One meal document per day holds a slots map (spine C3); auto-indexing every subfield multiplies write cost for queries nobody makes.
COST. The running totals on the same document.
COST. Portfolio blocks are a large ordered array rendered as a unit and never queried into.

COST. plates is a map with roughly 1,100 leaf paths; every auto-indexed subfield is an index-entry write on every rollup, and the document approaches the 40,000-entry ceiling. No query reads these fields individually.
COST. The week grocery list is an array nobody queries into.

PDPL. G9 requires NINE exemptions across cycle and periods; two were deployed and seven were not, so five cycle fields and two period fields were being auto-indexed in a deployed project. PHASE2-ACCEPTANCE.md recorded this as 'six missing' by counting three checkins rows that belong to G3, not G9. Each row below closes one real cross-user query. This one: recentStarts is the rolling list of her last cycle start dates, and an index on it makes 'find every woman whose cycle started in week N' executable.
PDPL. mode is datesAndSymptoms or symptomsOnly. Indexed, it segments the women who declined to share dates — which is precisely the choice the mode exists to let her make privately.

PDPL. Her stated cycle length. An indexed integer in the 21-45 range is a queryable medical attribute, and 'everyone with a cycle shorter than 24 days' is a clinical cohort nobody in this company should be able to assemble.
PDPL. The sharing grants. Indexing consent state makes 'every woman sharing symptoms with a coach' a query, which turns a private decision into a marketable segment.
PDPL. Her most recent period. The single most sensitive scalar in the product; an index on it answers 'who is bleeding today' across every user.
PDPL. The end date of a period entry. periods.start was exempted and end was not, which left half the range queryable — enough to reconstruct the other half.
PDPL. stillBleeding is a boolean that is true for exactly the women currently on their period. Of every field in this file, this is the one an index most directly weaponises.

COST. The recipe list screen is answered by ONE document, `recipeIndex/{locale}_v{N}`, not by a query across `recipes`. A query returning N recipes on every Eat open is N reads per open: at 200 recipes, 10,000 women and three opens a day that is about $360 a day. Exempting the fields the index document already answers makes the expensive shape unexecutable rather than merely discouraged, which is the same posture the RULE 11 exemptions above take.

S16 TTL. A liveness session is single use and dead after CHALLENGE_TTL_SEC; Firestore TTL deletes it from expiresAt. Never queried on, so automatic indexing is off as well.

S16 TTL. A verification job gets expireAt only once it is decided (config.DECIDED_RECORD_RETENTION_DAYS, pending counsel). A job still waiting on a review has none and is never swept. Never queried on.
S16 TTL. A review flag gets expireAt only when it leaves PENDING_REVIEW (decided or expired). nidRegistry and verificationReviewAccess deliberately have no TTL. Never queried on.
W1 TTL. A waitlist entry is deleted 180 days after she joined (pending counsel); it exists only to send one message when Own Hub opens. Never queried on.
W1 TTL. The per-IP daily counter for the waitlist is deleted after two days. Never queried on.
